sections.name: Learn quantum computing
sections.intro: From first principles to running circuits, with no physics background assumed.

items.title: IBM Quantum Learning
items.note: Free courses from basics to algorithms, with Qiskit notebooks. The most direct route to running your first circuit.

items.title: PennyLane Codebook
items.note: Short coding exercises that build intuition gate by gate.

items.title: Quantum Country
items.note: An introduction to quantum computing built to be remembered, with spaced-repetition questions.

items.title: Quantum algorithms for data analysis
items.note: Rigorous lecture notes, including a chapter on quantum Monte Carlo.

items.title: Physics 219: quantum computation
items.note: The classic Caltech graduate course, with lecture notes, for readers who want the theory in depth.

sections.name: Research on quantum finance
sections.intro: The papers behind the verdicts and horizons in Veqctor. Start with a review, then the pricing line.

items.title: Quantum computing for finance
items.by: Herman et al., Nature Reviews Physics, 2023
items.note: The most complete recent survey of algorithms and use cases.

items.title: Quantum computing for finance: state-of-the-art and future prospects
items.note: IBM's view of pricing, risk and optimisation use cases.

items.title: Quantum computing for finance: overview and prospects
items.note: An early, accessible overview of the field.

items.title: Quantum speedup of Monte Carlo methods
items.note: Where the quadratic Monte Carlo speed-up is established in general.

items.title: Quantum amplitude amplification and estimation
items.note: The original amplitude estimation algorithm.

items.title: Quantum computational finance: Monte Carlo pricing of financial derivatives
items.by: Rebentrost, Gupt and Bromley, Phys. Rev. A, 2018
items.note: First application of amplitude estimation to option pricing.

items.title: Option pricing using quantum computers
items.note: Circuits for European, Asian and basket options, run on IBM hardware.

items.title: Quantum risk analysis
items.by: Woerner and Egger, npj Quantum Information, 2019
items.note: VaR and CVaR by amplitude estimation.

items.title: Credit risk analysis using quantum computers
items.by: Egger et al., IEEE Trans. Computers, 2021
items.note: Economic capital for a credit portfolio with a Gaussian factor model.

items.title: A threshold for quantum advantage in derivative pricing
items.note: The resource estimate behind 'about 7,500 logical qubits' for autocalls and TARFs.

items.title: How to factor 2048-bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits
items.note: Why post-quantum migration is urgent even though useful pricing is not.

sections.name: Software
sections.intro: Open-source libraries for classical reference models and for quantum circuits.

items.title: QuantLib
items.note: The reference open-source library for pricing and risk. Veqctor's kits are tested against it.

items.title: Implementing QuantLib
items.note: How QuantLib is designed, by its lead maintainer.

items.title: Qiskit
items.note: The most widely used SDK; runs on simulators and IBM hardware.

items.title: Qiskit Finance
items.note: Distribution loading, option payoffs and portfolio problems for Qiskit.

items.title: PennyLane
items.note: Differentiable programming, suited to variational methods and quantum machine learning.

items.title: CUDA-Q
items.note: Fast GPU simulation and hybrid quantum-classical workflows.

items.title: Cirq
items.note: Google's framework for writing and simulating circuits.

items.title: Quirk
items.note: Drag-and-drop circuits in the browser with live state display. The fastest way to build intuition.

sections.name: Run on simulators and hardware
sections.intro: Cloud access to real quantum processors and emulators. Most offer a free tier or credits for small experiments.

items.title: IBM Quantum Platform
items.note: Free monthly time on real IBM processors, plus the visual Composer for building circuits.

items.title: Amazon Braket
items.note: One account for trapped ions, neutral atoms and superconducting machines from several vendors.

items.title: Azure Quantum
items.note: Hardware access and documentation for the Q# ecosystem.

items.title: Quantum resource estimator
items.note: Estimates logical and physical qubits and run time for an algorithm: the basis of a go or no-go.

items.title: OVHcloud Quantum Platform
items.note: European cloud access to emulators and quantum processors, for teams with sovereignty constraints.

sections.name: Model risk and regulation
sections.intro: The frameworks any model, classical or quantum, has to satisfy before use in a bank.

items.title: SR 11-7: Guidance on model risk management
items.note: The reference text on model development, validation and governance.

items.title: ECB guide to internal models (revised July 2025)
items.note: Supervisory expectations for internal models in the euro area, with links to the guide.

items.title: SS1/23: Model risk management principles for banks
items.note: The UK principles, in force since May 2024.

items.title: Post-quantum cryptography standards
items.note: FIPS 203, 204 and 205, published in 2024: the basis of every post-quantum migration plan.
